title: Quantifying Biogenic Silica Deposition Rates Adapted Method
author: Brittany N Zepernick
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.72vhqe6

steps.title: Filter Selection and Sample Collection
steps.instruction: Select the appropriate polycarbonate filter size based on the target organism (e.g., 0.22 µm for environmental samples to collect all potential diatoms, or 2.0 µm for axenic cultures).

steps.title: Vacuum Filtration of Samples
steps.instruction: Vacuum filter the designated volume of culture or environmental sample onto the filter. Volume depends on initial culture volume and biomass (previous experiments used 10 mL to 100 mL).

substeps.instruction: Filter all replicates in a corresponding treatment simultaneously to minimize error.
Turn off the vacuum and release the pressure once filtration is complete.

steps.title: External PDMPO Wash
steps.instruction: Wash the filters to remove external PDMPO that could interfere with calculations.

substeps.instruction: Turn off the vacuum.
Add 20 mL of sterile growth media (for cultures) or 0.22 µm filtered sample water (for environmental samples) onto the filters.
Turn the vacuum on and filter the volume through (Rinse 1).
Ensure no liquid remains around the internal lid of the filter tulip to avoid dilution in the next step.
Turn the vacuum off and release built-up pressure.

steps.title: Acid Treatment
steps.instruction: Treat the filters with hydrochloric acid to prepare for osmotic lysing.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 mL of 10% HCl onto the filters.
Incubate for 00:02:00.
Turn the vacuum on and filter through.
While the vacuum is still on, rinse the internal lip of the filter tulip with Milli-Q water to remove all remaining acid.
Once acid is completely removed, turn the vacuum off and release pressure.

steps.title: Osmotic Lysing of Cells
steps.instruction: Lyse the diatom cells to release PDMPO stored in the silica deposition vesicle.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 mL of Milli-Q water (resistivity ≥ 18 Ω-cm).
Incubate for 00:02:00.
Turn the vacuum on until all Milli-Q has been pulled through.
Turn the vacuum off.

steps.title: Final Rinse and Storage
steps.instruction: Perform a final rinse and preserve the samples.

substeps.instruction: Perform a final rinse of 20 mL sterile media or filtered environmental water, ensuring filters are equally covered.
Turn vacuum on until liquid is pulled through, then turn vacuum off.
Using sterile tweezers, fold filters into quarters and place in labeled 2 mL cryovials.
Flash freeze in liquid nitrogen immediately and store at -80 °C.

steps.title: Sample Preparation for Digestion
steps.instruction: Prepare reagents and thaw samples for frustule digestion.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1L stocks of 0.2 M NaOH and 1 M HCl.
Thaw samples on ice.
Remove filters from cryovials and transfer them to 15 mL labeled Falcon tubes.

steps.title: Frustule Digestion
steps.instruction: Digest the diatom frustules using a hot alkaline solution.

substeps.instruction: Add 4 mL of 0.2 M NaOH to all tubes, ensuring filters are fully submerged.
Mix gently by hand to remove air bubbles around the filter.
Screw Falcon tube lids on to prevent evaporation.
Place tubes in an 80 °C water bath and incubate in the dark for 01:00:00.
Remove tubes from the water bath and cool in an ice bath for 00:15:00.

steps.title: Neutralization and Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Neutralize the digested samples and prepare for fluorescence reading.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 1 M HCl to each tube (resulting in a net volume of 5 mL).
Invert tubes and hand mix thoroughly.
Centrifuge tubes at 13,000 rpm for 00:05:00 to remove filter fragments and remaining cells.

steps.title: Standard Curve Establishment
steps.instruction: Establish a standard curve of 5 different concentrations prior to reading sample fluorescence.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 4 mL NaOH samples that have been incubated at 80 °C in the water bath with the experimental samples.
Chill on ice and neutralize with 1 mL 1 M HCl.
Add selected volumes of PDMPO to the neutralized matrix.
Include a blank consisting only of the NaOH-HCl matrix without PDMPO.
